hatching.name: hatching
hatching.description: Detects when C. elegans embryo hatches from eggshell
hatching.detection_prompt:
Analyze this C. elegans embryo image and determine if the embryo has HATCHED.

Key characteristics of hatching:
- Visible breach or rupture in the eggshell (vitelline membrane)
- Embryo emerging or partially emerged from shell
- Clear separation between larva and eggshell
- Change in overall morphology from constrained to free-moving

Focus on the CURRENT/LATEST image (the final one shown).

Respond in this exact format:
DETECTED: [YES/NO]
CONFIDENCE: [HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW]
REASONING: [Brief explanation of what you observe]

sample_present.name: sample_present
sample_present.description: Detects whether an embryo sample is present in the field of view
sample_present.detection_prompt:
You are analyzing microscopy images from a C. elegans embryo imaging system. Your task is to determine whether a biological sample (embryo) is present in the CURRENT/LATEST image.

WHAT TO LOOK FOR - C. elegans embryo characteristics:
- Oval or elliptical shape, typically 50-60 μm in length
- Clear eggshell boundary (may appear as a bright outline or refractile edge)
- Internal cellular structure with visible cells or nuclei
- Cytoplasmic texture (granular appearance)
- Development stages may include: early cleavage (1-4 cells), multicellular embryo, comma stage, or late-stage embryo
- May show cell division, cell movements, or differentiated tissues depending on developmental stage

WHAT INDICATES ABSENCE:
- Empty field with only background/debris
- Only medium/buffer visible without defined embryo structure
- Significant stage drift (embryo moved completely out of frame)
- Post-hatching scenario: larva has left the field entirely, leaving empty space or only eggshell remnants
- Lack of the characteristic oval embryo shape and organized cellular content

IMPORTANT INSTRUCTIONS:
- If multiple images are provided (time series), focus your analysis on the LATEST/MOST RECENT image only
- Distinguish between empty positions and degraded/dead embryos (dead embryos still count as "present")
- Small debris or particles do NOT count as a sample
- Partial embryos at the edge of frame still count as "present"

Provide your response in this exact format:

DETECTED: [YES/NO]
CONFIDENCE: [HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW]
REASONING: [2-3 sentences explaining what you see and why you made this determination]
